cards: Louis XIV was King of France from 1643 to 1715, whose long reign marked the height of royal absolutism.
John Locke was an English philosopher whose Two Treatises of Government and Essay Concerning Human Understanding, published around 1689, shaped liberal political thought and empiricism.
Aurangzeb was the sixth Mughal emperor, reigning from 1658 to 1707.
Oliver Cromwell was an English soldier and politician who rose to command the New Model Army in the Civil Wars against Charles I and supported the king's execution in 1649.
Shivaji (1630–1680) was the founder of the Maratha state in western India and was crowned Chhatrapati in 1674.
James VI and I was king of Scotland as James VI from 1567 and king of England and Ireland as James I from 1603 until his death in 1625.
Johannes Kepler was a German astronomer and mathematician, born in the imperial city of Weil der Stadt, who discovered the three laws of planetary motion.
Albrecht von Wallenstein was a Bohemian nobleman who raised and commanded the imperial armies in the Thirty Years' War.
Charles X Gustav was king of Sweden in the mid-seventeenth century and a gifted military commander.
Galileo Galilei was an Italian astronomer, physicist and mathematician whose telescopic discoveries of 1609–1610, including the moons of Jupiter and the phases of Venus, supported the Copernican…
Gustavus Adolphus was King of Sweden who reigned from 1611 to 1632.
Jean-Baptiste Colbert was a minister of Louis XIV of France who directed finance, commerce and the navy.
Nurhaci was a Jurchen chieftain who unified the Jurchen clans of Manchuria between 1583 and 1616 and laid the foundations of the Qing Empire.
Shah Jahan was the fifth Mughal emperor, ruling from 1628 to 1658.
Frederick V was Elector Palatine and the leading Calvinist prince of the Holy Roman Empire.
Hugo Grotius was a seventeenth-century Dutch jurist, a founder of modern international law.
Isaac Newton was an English mathematician and physicist, one of the central figures of the Scientific Revolution.
Jahangir was the fourth Mughal emperor, reigning from 1605 to 1627.
The Kangxi Emperor was one of the longest-reigning rulers in Chinese history, governing the Qing Empire from 1661 to 1722.
Samuel de Champlain was a French explorer, navigator and colonial administrator who founded Quebec in 1608.
Wu Sangui was a Ming general who commanded the defences at Shanhai Pass in 1644.
Abbas I of Persia, known as Shah Abbas the Great, was the most celebrated ruler of the Safavid Empire, reigning from 1588 to 1629.
Cardinal Richelieu was a French clergyman and statesman who was chief minister of Louis XIII from 1624 until his death.
Charles II of England was king of England, Scotland and Ireland, restored to the throne in 1660 after the Commonwealth.
Charles XI was king of Sweden in the late seventeenth century.
Gaspar de Guzmán, Count-Duke of Olivares
Gaspar de Guzmán, Count-Duke of Olivares, was the chief minister of Philip IV of Spain from 1621 to 1643.
James II of England, also James VII of Scotland, was King of England, Scotland and Ireland from 1685 to 1688.
Baruch Spinoza was a Dutch philosopher from Amsterdam's Portuguese Jewish community, which expelled him in 1656.
Christiaan Huygens was a Dutch mathematician, physicist and astronomer.
John Churchill, 1st Duke of Marlborough, was an English general and statesman who commanded the allied armies against France in the War of the Spanish Succession.
René Descartes was a French philosopher and mathematician who spent most of his working life in the Dutch Republic.
The 5th Dalai Lama, Ngawang Lobsang Gyatso, was the first Dalai Lama to hold political power over all Tibet.
Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was a Dutch draper and self-taught scientist of Delft.
Charles I was King of England, Scotland and Ireland from 1625 to 1649.
Frederick William, Elector of Brandenburg, known as the Great Elector, ruled Brandenburg-Prussia from 1640.
Hong Taiji was the son and successor of Nurhaci as leader of the Manchus.
Li Zicheng was the leader of a peasant rebellion that overthrew the Ming Empire.
Louis XIII, son of Henry IV, was king of France from 1610.
Shahaji Bhonsle was a Maratha general in the Deccan and father of Shivaji, founder of the Maratha kingdom.
Thomas Hobbes was an English philosopher whose Leviathan of 1651 is a founding work of modern political thought.
